clues: This place sits where a river meets a big bay, on flat land by the sea. The nation's capital, Washington, lies just a short drive west of here.
The wide bay beside this place softens its weather all year. Summers stay less hot than inland towns, and winter cold bites less hard here.
In 1694 a royal governor moved the seat of rule to this small port town. He gave the town a new name then, one it still keeps.
Sailboats fill the harbor of this place, home to a famed school for sea officers. Each year it hosts the world's largest boat show held on the water.
Maryland's lawmakers and governor do the work of the state in this place. Its old State House stands at the heart of town.
